recap.text: Carl slips off to the personal space and opens the Cookbook's chapter on portals. A note by Crawler Milk, from the sixth edition, finds them hard to understand: dozens of types, some that drag you in if you go slack. A portal the size of a button can toss you into a monster den, and teleport traps are the worst. Carl adds a note about brands of portals.

Lucia Mar has set one teleport trap just inside the saferoom door and another just outside the guildhall's. Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on the Sledge and sends the two automatons in one after the other, using the loophole that the real trap module sits outside, at the destination. The first triggers the trap and appears among the hunters. The second rushes at Lucia with a beanie baby on its shoulder, a black cat thing in a crown and sunglasses.

Astrid can call one to three club guards with every casting, so Carl sets two-part teleport traps down the hallway to send any NPC who trips them to a locked closet. He fixes anchors to three fist-sized spider automatons and throws Samantha across the street to release them. He teleports onto one and crushes it, then brings Donut's totems to him through the traps.

Carl pulls out the teleport automatons, each holding the second half of a trap, then puts most away because the traps glittering before the castle are too thick for a larger force. He keeps out Katia's, Imani's, Holger's and Splash Zone's, and messages those four to come in. Katia, Imani and Splash Zone appear. Holger's trap brings Dong Quixote, mounted on Gonk, the swamp yak that once belonged to King Rust, because Holger gave Dong his half.

beats.headline: The worst of the portals
beats.text: Carl slips off to the personal space and opens the Cookbook's chapter on portals. A note by Crawler Milk, from the sixth edition, finds them hard to understand: dozens of types that work in different ways. Some are like doors you never notice, some work at a touch, some drag you in if you go slack, though you can still break free. Sometimes you must be big enough to fit, and sometimes a portal the size of a button tosses you into a monster den. Teleport traps are the worst. Carl adds a note about the different brands of portals, but has no time to write more.
beats.gist: Carl reads Crawler Milk's note calling teleport traps the worst of dozens of confusing portals.

beats.headline: Lucia's two traps
beats.text: Lucia Mar has set at least two teleport traps, one just inside the saferoom door and one just outside the guildhall's. According to some kid at the panel, the system allows them in saferooms because the real trap module is set outside, at the destination: a loophole that has been around for years. Carl's plan uses it. Donut casts Clockwork Triplicate on the Sledge and sends the two automatons in one after the other. The first triggers the trap and appears right outside among the hunters. The second rushes at Lucia with what looks like Donut on its shoulder, but is one of Bautista's beanie babies, a black cat thing in a crown and sunglasses.
beats.gist: Lucia Mar's saferoom trap sends Donut's two automatons out; the second charges her carrying a beanie baby.

beats.headline: Traps for summoned guards
beats.text: Astrid can call one to three club guards to her with every casting, no cooldown, so the ambush needs a contingency, and Carl takes a page from Lucia Mar's playbook. Down the hallway to the monster door he sets his two-part teleport traps, to send any NPC who trips them to a locked closet on the top floor. Astrid flies everywhere and will not trip them, but he calls out fairies specifically, in case she slams into one on purpose. The second halves, the beacons, still have to go upstairs into the hidden utility closet.
beats.gist: Carl sets teleport traps down the hallway to send tripped NPCs to a locked top-floor closet.

beats.headline: Anchors on spider automatons
beats.text: Samantha asks why Carl does not do what the scary lady does, and he could kiss her. He has four sets of two-part teleport traps; the market has one more. Into Samantha's neck hole go three fist-sized spider automatons, each with an anchor half fixed to its flat top, and a red one carrying a trap Donut set. Mordecai objects that one trapper must set both halves, or crawlers would trade anchors through the guild rooms. That is the point, says Carl: the anchor rides the automaton, and the automaton can go anywhere. He arms the triggers in the clearing, slips his last anchor into Samantha, and throws her. She lands across the street and lets the spiders out.
beats.gist: Carl throws Samantha across the street after loading her with three anchor-carrying spider automatons.

beats.headline: Totems through the traps
beats.text: Carl teleports onto the spider automaton across the street from the capitol building and crushes it under his weight. The other three, two regular and the red one, scatter; the fourth stays inside Samantha. In the room where the floor began, Ren and Quan are fighting. Donut is far away in her own fight with the duendes, with her deck, so she can summon totems, and through the teleport traps Carl can bring them to him. With luck Quan cannot snare them, and they can attack him without first getting past his own totems. It is an exploit, and a chickenshit one. Jola fills the left of the room and Lazarus appears on the right, the spider automaton under him crunching in a shower of sparks.
beats.gist: Carl teleports onto a spider automaton, crushes it, and brings Donut's totems to him through the traps.

beats.headline: Both halves on one robot
beats.text: On the roof of a block of penthouses, a demon stands in the shell of the snake city boss. Carl sets his last automaton down in front of the door. This one carries both halves of a teleport trap. It will walk up and bump the snake, setting it off, and because the anchor rides on the same robot, the snake will go nowhere, though it still technically teleports. That should break the demon out of the shell, and out of Sister Ines's control; done properly, the nun has to die first.
beats.gist: Carl sets his last automaton, carrying both trap halves, before the door to teleport the snake nowhere.

beats.headline: Into Samantha
beats.text: Forty-five seconds. Carl tells Samantha not to let him out until the fire flares, and she wants to know why he is yelling; she is having a tussle. Behind him Raul groans while Alpha Carl berates him. Carl pulls the teleport trap's trigger out of his inventory and steps into it, and he arrives at the trap he left inside Samantha.
beats.gist: Carl steps into the teleport trap's trigger and arrives at the trap he left inside Samantha.

beats.headline: Four automatons out
beats.text: The ground before the castle glitters with thousands of traps, far thicker than Carl expected, and he means to collect any summon traps on the way. From his inventory he pulls the teleport automatons, each carrying the second half of a trap, then puts most of them away: the traps here are too thick for a larger force. He keeps out only Katia's, Imani's, Holger's and Splash Zone's, and messages those four to come in. Katia, Imani and Splash Zone appear. The trap meant for Holger brings Dong Quixote instead, mounted on Gonk, the swamp yak that once belonged to King Rust: Holger gave Dong his half of the trap.
beats.gist: Carl calls four teleport automatons in, but Holger's trap brings Dong Quixote on Gonk instead.
